title: Three Switches Turn Grip Into Crawling

scenes.visual: Reuses the first film's exact colour map and side-view adhesion cross-section: amber matrix (#D4A359) below, slate-blue membrane (#5C7A99), extended teal alpha (#2EC4B6) and coral beta (#FF6B6B) integrins, violet talin (#9B72CF), magenta vinculin (#E85D9E) and gently drifting silver-white actin (#E2E8F0). Title 'Three Switches Turn Grip Into Crawling' fades across upper frame (size 38) and clears at 2.0 s.

scenes.tts: The first film showed how integrins switch grip from inside and build force-sensing adhesions. Yet a grip alone just anchors a cell, so how do switches shape actin to make it crawl? Three small switches of the Rho family run the actin skeleton.
scenes.caption: The first film showed how integrins switch grip from inside and build force-sensing adhesions. Yet a grip alone just anchors a cell, so how do switches shape actin to make it crawl? Three small switches of the Rho family run the actin skeleton.
scenes.visual: The side-view adhesion cross-section from the first film smoothly tilts and pulls back into a top-down view of a single rounded fibroblast resting on the same amber matrix (#D4A359), filling 65% of the frame height. Glowing teal-and-coral dots beneath the cell mark its integrin focal adhesions, while faint silver-white actin filaments drift inside.
scenes.narration: The first film showed how integrins switch grip from inside and build force-sensing adhesions. Yet a grip alone just anchors a cell, so how do switches shape actin to make it crawl? Three small switches of the Rho family run the actin skeleton.

scenes.tts: Like Ras, Rho, Rac and C D C forty-two flip between two states. Bound to GTP, a switch is on and engages its effectors. Bound to GDP, it is off. Exchange factors swap GDP for GTP to turn a switch on. G T P ase activating proteins speed its own GTP splitting, which turns it off.
scenes.caption: Like Ras, Rho, Rac and Cdc42 flip between two states. Bound to GTP, a switch is on and engages its effectors. Bound to GDP, it is off. Exchange factors swap GDP for GTP to turn a switch on. GTPase-activating proteins speed its own GTP splitting, which turns it off.
scenes.visual: Above the same fibroblast, a compact glowing toggle badge flips between muted 'GDP · off' and bright 'GTP · on' as small arrows labelled 'GEF' (on) and 'GAP' (off; speeds GTP splitting) cycle beside it. Three coloured switch tokens appear along the top edge: crimson 'Rho' (#F87171), emerald 'Rac' (#34D399), and sky-blue 'Cdc42' (#60A5FA). Corner label: 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Like Ras, Rho, Rac and Cdc42 flip between two states. Bound to GTP, a switch is on and engages its effectors. Bound to GDP, it is off. Exchange factors swap GDP for GTP to turn a switch on. GTPase-activating proteins speed its own GTP splitting, which turns it off.

scenes.tts: Switch Rho on in a resting fibroblast, and thick contractile cables span the cell. These are stress fibres, bundles of actin and myosin two anchored at focal adhesions. Rho activates Rho kinase, which raises myosin two activity so the cables contract and pull.
scenes.caption: Switch Rho on in a resting fibroblast, and thick contractile cables span the cell. These are stress fibres, bundles of actin and myosin II anchored at focal adhesions. Rho activates Rho kinase, which raises myosin II activity so the cables contract and pull.
scenes.visual: The crimson 'Rho · GTP' token pulses brightly. Inside the same fibroblast, silver-white actin bundles align into thick parallel cables accented with crimson myosin II bars (#F87171) running between enlarged teal-and-coral adhesion dots. A compact side callout glows: 'Rho → Rho kinase (ROCK) → myosin II'. The cables visibly draw taut and pull inward.
scenes.narration: Switch Rho on in a resting fibroblast, and thick contractile cables span the cell. These are stress fibres, bundles of actin and myosin II anchored at focal adhesions. Rho activates Rho kinase, which raises myosin II activity so the cables contract and pull.

scenes.tts: Now switch to Rac. Active Rac pushes out a broad, thin sheet at the cell edge called a lamellipodium. Rac turns on the WAVE complex, which activates Arp two-three. Arp two-three starts each new actin filament as a branch on an older one.
scenes.caption: Now switch to Rac. Active Rac pushes out a broad, thin sheet at the cell edge called a lamellipodium. Rac turns on the WAVE complex, which activates Arp2/3. Arp2/3 starts each new actin filament as a branch on an older one.
scenes.visual: The crimson stress fibres soften as the emerald 'Rac · GTP' token lights up. The cell's right rim billows outward into a broad emerald-tinted sheet labelled 'lamellipodium' (#34D399) filled with branching silver-white actin trees growing against the edge. Compact callout: 'Rac → WAVE → Arp2/3'.
scenes.narration: Now switch to Rac. Active Rac pushes out a broad, thin sheet at the cell edge called a lamellipodium. Rac turns on the WAVE complex, which activates Arp2/3. Arp2/3 starts each new actin filament as a branch on an older one.

scenes.tts: Third comes C D C forty-two. It is best known for triggering filopodia, thin fingers with cores of parallel filaments that probe the surface ahead. Other proteins, mainly formins, build those parallel cores. Separately, C D C forty-two opens folded WASP-family proteins, freeing them to activate Arp two-three.
scenes.caption: Third comes Cdc42. It is best known for triggering filopodia, thin fingers with cores of parallel filaments that probe the surface ahead. Other proteins, mainly formins, build those parallel cores. Separately, Cdc42 opens folded WASP-family proteins, freeing them to activate Arp2/3.
scenes.visual: The sky-blue 'Cdc42 · GTP' token lights up. Slender sky-blue spikes labelled 'filopodia' (#60A5FA) with straight parallel actin cores (small label 'cores built mainly by formins') extend past the rim to probe the amber matrix, while a small inset shows a folded WASP block unfolding when Cdc42-GTP binds (callout: 'Cdc42 → WASP/N-WASP → Arp2/3').
scenes.narration: Third comes Cdc42. It is best known for triggering filopodia, thin fingers with cores of parallel filaments that probe the surface ahead. Other proteins, mainly formins, build those parallel cores. Separately, Cdc42 opens folded WASP-family proteins, freeing them to activate Arp2/3.

scenes.tts: Adhesions and switches are wired together. Proteins phosphorylated by focal adhesion kinase and Src recruit exchange factors that turn Rac on. A fresh grip at the front therefore calls for more pushing there. Put the steps in order: push with Rac, grip with integrins, pull with Rho.
scenes.caption: Adhesions and switches are wired together. Proteins phosphorylated by focal adhesion kinase and Src recruit exchange factors that turn Rac on. A fresh grip at the front therefore calls for more pushing there. Put the steps in order: push with Rac, grip with integrins, pull with Rho.
scenes.visual: The fibroblast polarises left-to-right across the amber matrix. At the right (front) edge, emerald Rac pushes out a lamellipodium; new teal/coral adhesions form beneath it, flashing cyan FAK-Src sparks that feed more emerald Rac. Behind them, crimson Rho stress fibres assemble to haul the body rightward. Labels appear in order: '1 Push', '2 Grip', '3 Pull'.
scenes.narration: Adhesions and switches are wired together. Proteins phosphorylated by focal adhesion kinase and Src recruit exchange factors that turn Rac on. A fresh grip at the front therefore calls for more pushing there. Put the steps in order: push with Rac, grip with integrins, pull with Rho.

scenes.tts: One step is still missing. Suppose a crawling cell locks its integrins tightly at both front and back. None of its old adhesions can come apart. When Rho and myosin two contract the cell body, what happens?
scenes.caption: One step is still missing. Suppose a crawling cell locks its integrins tightly at both front and back. None of its old adhesions can come apart. When Rho and myosin II contract the cell body, what happens?
scenes.visual: Bright gold clamps lock both the front and rear teal/coral adhesions onto the amber matrix. Crimson stress fibres tense across the cell body, straining without moving the rear edge. Question card fades in at top: 'Front and back adhesions stay locked. What happens when Rho pulls?'
scenes.narration: One step is still missing. Suppose a crawling cell locks its integrins tightly at both front and back. None of its old adhesions can come apart. When Rho and myosin II contract the cell body, what happens?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause: the question stays on screen at full contrast while crimson stress fibres quiver under tension between the locked front and rear adhesions on the amber matrix; a subtle circular progress ring sweeps across 4.5 seconds.

scenes.tts: The cell stalls in place. To move forward, old adhesions at the back must come apart so the tail draws in. Push, grip, pull, let go: that cycle moves the cell. Rac in front and Rho behind is a simplification. Sensors of Rho activity in living cells find some at the front too.
scenes.caption: The cell stalls in place. To move forward, old adhesions at the back must come apart so the tail draws in. Push, grip, pull, let go: that cycle moves the cell. Rac in front and Rho behind is a simplification. Sensors of Rho activity in living cells find some at the front too.
scenes.visual: Question clears. Rear gold locks dissolve and back teal/coral adhesions fade apart ('4 Let go'). Crimson stress fibres shorten immediately, gliding the cell smoothly rightward across the amber matrix while a small honest crimson pulse also glimmers along the emerald leading edge ('Rho also active at front').
scenes.narration: The cell stalls in place. To move forward, old adhesions at the back must come apart so the tail draws in. Push, grip, pull, let go: that cycle moves the cell. Rac in front and Rho behind is a simplification. Sensors of Rho activity in living cells find some at the front too.

scenes.tts: Rho, Rac and C D C forty-two shape actin to turn grip into crawling. Rac pushes broad sheets, C D C forty-two probes with fingers, and Rho contracts cables against adhesions. Break the grip or the switches, and this kind of crawling stalls.
scenes.caption: Rho, Rac and Cdc42 shape actin to turn grip into crawling. Rac pushes broad sheets, Cdc42 probes with fingers, and Rho contracts cables against adhesions. Break the grip or the switches, and this kind of crawling stalls.
scenes.visual: The fibroblast completes one clean stride across the amber matrix with all colours harmonised: emerald front sheet, sky-blue probing tips, teal/coral adhesions assembling under the front and dissolving at the back, crimson contractile cables hauling the body forward. Smooth fade to slate before end card.
scenes.narration: Rho, Rac and Cdc42 shape actin to turn grip into crawling. Rac pushes broad sheets, Cdc42 probes with fingers, and Rho contracts cables against adhesions. Break the grip or the switches, and this kind of crawling stalls.

scenes.visual: End card on deep-slate background, high contrast, single line only with no smaller line underneath: 'Rho, Rac and Cdc42 shape actin to turn grip into crawling.'
